From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Subject: Brightline pilot — temporary GPU runway & autoscale exception request

Team —

Quick summary: Brightline is ready to run a 10-day production pilot (customer-facing slot) that will generate consistent low-latency traffic during a 6-hour daily window. They need a temporary dedicated runway to avoid cold-start latency and reduce token cost risk.

What I'm asking for (short):
- Reserve a carve of 8 x A100-equivalent GPU slots for the pilot window (10 days, tentative start 2026-07-06)
- Approve an autoscale policy exception so the carve doesn't get evicted under normal pool autoscale thresholds
- Ramp and canary rules: 50% traffic day 1, 100% by day 3; fallback routing to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained

Why this matters: Brightline is a strategic partner — this pilot could convert into a Dedicated contract. They have sensitive latency targets; failing the first week due to preemption would likely sink the deal.

Attached: brightline-pilot-maf.xlsx (mutual action plan), pilot-architecture.pdf (topology + fallback options), and a draft MOU (mou-draft-brightline.docx).

Operational asks for product/ops:
- Kimberly: can you confirm SLA/GPU-slice gating implications for Q3 reserve lanes?
- Marcus: what is the minimal carve we can guarantee without violating existing reserved commitments?
- Neha/Priyom: any downstream autoscale or billing policy impacts we should flag to sales/legal?

I propose a 30-minute sync today to lock the runway and sign off on the canary plan. 

Thanks,
Logan

--
Logan Wright

Subject: Re: Brightline pilot — temporary GPU runway & autoscale exception request

Thanks for the clear ask, Logan. I skimmed the MAF and architecture PDF. A few immediate thoughts:

- We can technically carve 8 slots for 10 days, but we need to reconcile that with the reserve window on 2026-07-08 for the Atlas sprint (we have a product commit). If that sprint's reservation is firm, we'll need an ops-approved soft-eviction window.
- Please confirm the exact GPU class (A100 vs. A10x) and whether Brightline accepts quantized fallback for 25% of requests during degraded capacity.
- Billing note: temporary carve will be billed as "pilot-reserve" at a discounted rate; we need legal to approve the language in the MOU about credits if preemption occurs.

Operational checklist (for the sync):
1) Exact start/end timestamps for the carve
2) Canary traffic ramp plan and health metrics (p95 latency target, error budget)
3) Autoscale exception TTL (we prefer 7 days; you requested 10)
4) Fallback model variants and associated perf profiles

I can join a sync at 11:30 PST today. @Marcus — can you pull a quick commit map of reservations for 7/6–7/16 and share the risk windows?

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Capacity Operations — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Diane Park <diane@brightline.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline pilot — temporary GPU runway & autoscale exception request

Thanks — pulled the reservation map. Quick reality check:

- Existing Q3 commitments: we have 24 GPU-slice-days reserved across Atlas and Nova between 7/7–7/10 (soft) and a firm 16-slice commitment on 7/12 for a launch. We can carve 8 slots for Brightline for 7/06–7/14 with the following constraints:
  * The carve must be a soft carve with elevated preemption threshold only between 11:00–17:00 PST daily (Brightline's preferential window)
  * We can set an explicit autoscale exception TTL of 9 days (7/06 00:00 to 7/15 23:59). TTL extension needs Ops + Product sign-off

Alternate mitigations if full carve isn't acceptable:
- Pre-warm strategy: keep 8 GPUs warm but in shared mode; autoscale would still reclaim them if firm commitments arrive but pre-warm reduces cold-start by ~70%
- Burst lane: allow Brightline to use burst capacity for their 6-hour window up to a hard cap (12 GPUs) with strict throttles outside the window

Technical caveats:
- If we allow quantized fallback for 25% of requests, we can cut the effective GPU footprint by ~30% and increase headroom.
- Networking: the pilot needs an IP allowlist and VPC route punch for warm connections; that will take configuration ops time (~2–4 hours)

I'll attach the raw reservation CSV to the ticket (INF-3421). If everyone agrees, I'll schedule the soft carve and set the autoscale exception TTL to 9 days.

Marcus

- Sign the MOU with the credit clause for preemption. Please send the doc with redline instructions; our legal can turn it around in 48 hours.
- Ops note: we'll provide the IP allowlist tomorrow morning at 09:00 PST.
